localChanges: **Two games in one process, proven.** `npm run test:isolation` builds two `Game`s, registers the turn loop against each, and checks 13 ways that they share nothing: registries, rule registries, engines, turns, the civ1 registries, entities, events, turn state and random streams.

That needed the last of Stage 3 first. `registerRules.ts` had moved, but the two `registerEvents.ts` files still bound handlers to the singleton `Engine`, so a fresh `Game` had no handlers at all and its turn loop would never start. `core-turn-based-game` takes a structural `{engine, rules, turn}` rather than importing `Game` — `Game` imports `Turn` from there, so depending on it would make a package cycle, and a structural type says more precisely what the package touches anyway.

**The rule-count assertion.** The conformance snapshot now records every registered rule counted by type — 1055 across 65 types. A missed `register` call, or one registering into a registry nothing reads, changes the fixture and names the rule that went missing. That is the failure this stage actually hit: `Start` would have read 0 instead of 2, rather than the run ending silently with exit code 0.

It sits outside the checksum, with the DTO digest and the stray-`Math.random` count, so that adding an instrument does not perturb the state comparison it exists to protect. The checksums are unchanged: 7d6b6b04 / 73a0cc05 / 3431063b.

The isolation test found one bug of its own worth noting: its checks were lazy closures evaluated at the end, so "b's event did not reach a" was read after a's own emit had happened. Measurements are captured at the point of measurement now.
